Ensure the device is Android 13+ and Health Connect is installed. After connecting in Integrations, tap “Import latest data” or open Dashboard so sync runs; sleep/activity then write to &#96;sleep_sessions&#96; / &#96;activity_daily&#96;.\\\\\\\\n- **Google Fit:** Requires OAuth and correct Android client config (see below). **Does not work in Expo Go**; use a development or preview build.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 2. For **EAS preview** the Android app must use a client that matches the **EAS-built** app, not your local debug keystore.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Step 1: Get the EAS preview keystore fingerprint (SHA-1)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFrom the project root:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\ncd app\\\\\\\\neas credentials\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Choose **Android** → **preview** (or the profile you use for preview).\\\\\\\\n- **View** or **Download** the keystore; from it, get the **SHA-1** fingerprint.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nOr:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- In [expo.dev](https://expo.dev) → your project → **Credentials** → Android → preview → see the keystore fingerprint (SHA-1).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nYou need this exact SHA-1 for the Google Cloud Android client.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Step 2: Create or update the Android OAuth client\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Open [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/) → your project (or create one).\\\\\\\\n2. **APIs \u0026 Services** → **Credentials**.\\\\\\\\n3. **Create credentials** → **OAuth client ID** (or edit the existing Android client used by the app).\\\\\\\\n4. Application type: **Android**.\\\\\\\\n5. OAuth PKCE Error - EAS Build Solution\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Issue\\\\\\\\n**Error**: &#96;AuthApiError: invalid request: both auth code and verifier should be non empty&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThis error occurs when the PKCE code verifier stored during OAuth initiation cannot be retrieved during code exchange.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Why This Happens in Development\\\\\\\\n- SecureStore behavior differs in Expo Go/development builds\\\\\\\\n- Storage context may not persist between OAuth initiation and callback\\\\\\\\n- Deep linking handling can be inconsistent in development mode\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Solution: Use EAS Build\\\\\\\\nOAuth PKCE flow works much more reliably in EAS production builds because:\\\\\\\\n1. ✅ SecureStore has full native support\\\\\\\\n2. ✅ Deep linking is properly configured\\\\\\\\n3. ✅ Storage persistence is guaranteed\\\\\\\\n4. ✅ Better error handling and logging\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Building with EAS\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 1. Ensure EAS is configured\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\ncd app\\\\\\\\neas build:configure\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2. Set up EAS secrets (if not already done)\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\neas secret:create --scope project --name EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL --value \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"your-url\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\neas secret:create --scope project --name EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY --value \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"your-key\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 3. Build for Android (development build)\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\neas build --platform android --profile development\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 4. Install on device/emulator\\\\\\\\nAfter build completes, install the APK and test OAuth.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Alternative: Development Workaround\\\\\\\\nIf you need to test OAuth in development mode, you can:\\\\\\\\n1. Use email/password authentication instead\\\\\\\\n2. Test OAuth only in EAS builds\\\\\\\\n3. Ensure the app doesn't restart between OAuth initiation and callback\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Expected Behavior in EAS Build\\\\\\\\n- OAuth flow should complete without code verifier errors\\\\\\\\n- Deep linking should work reliably\\\\\\\\n- Session should persist correctly\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Testing Checklist\\\\\\\\n- [ ] EAS build installed on device/emulator\\\\\\\\n- [ ] Google OAuth button works\\\\\\\\n- [ ] OAuth callback is received\\\\\\\\n- [ ] Session is created successfully\\\\\\\\n- [ ] User is navigated to app after sign-in\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"# OAuth PKCE Error - How to Get Sleep Data from Samsung Health and Save It\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Overview\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThis document explains the complete flow of how sleep data from Samsung Health is fetched, Provider** (&#96;app/src/lib/health/providers/samsungHealth.ts&#96;)\\\\\\\\n   - A provider class exists that can read sleep sessions from Samsung Health\\\\\\\\n   - It expects a native module called &#96;SamsungHealth&#96; to be available\\\\\\\\n   - The provider maps Samsung Health data to the unified &#96;SleepSession&#96; format\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n2. **Unified Health Service** (&#96;app/src/lib/health/unifiedService.ts&#96;)\\\\\\\\n   - Automatically selects the best available health provider\\\\\\\\n   - Provides a unified interface for fetching sleep data\\\\\\\\n   - Handles provider priority (Google Fit \u003e Health Connect \u003e Samsung Health)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n3. **Sync Function** (&#96;app/src/lib/sync.ts&#96;)\\\\\\\\n   - &#96;syncHealthData()&#96; function fetches latest sleep from the active provider\\\\\\\\n   - Calls &#96;upsertSleepSessionFromHealth()&#96; to save to Supabase\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n4. **Database Save Function** (&#96;app/src/lib/api.ts&#96;)\\\\\\\\n   - &#96;upsertSleepSessionFromHealth()&#96; saves sleep data to &#96;sleep_sessions&#96; table\\\\\\\\n   - Handles sleep stages, efficiency, heart rate, and other metadata\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n5. **UI Display** (&#96;app/src/screens/SleepScreen.tsx&#96;)\\\\\\\\n   - Shows last night's sleep data\\\\\\\\n   - Displays sleep stages (hypnogram)\\\\\\\\n   - Shows heart rate and body temperature if available\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### ⚠️ What's Missing\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. **Native Module**: The &#96;SamsungHealth&#96; native module is not implemented\\\\\\\\n OR a custom React Native bridge to Samsung Health APIs\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n2. **Current Workaround**: \\\\\\\\n   - Samsung Health data can be accessed **indirectly** through Google How to Get Sleep Data from Samsung Health and Save It\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Overview\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThis document explains the complete flow of how sleep data from Samsung Health is fetched, processed, and saved to your Supabase database so it can be viewed in the app.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Current State\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### ✅ What's Already Implemented\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. **Samsung Health Provider** (&#96;app/src/lib/health/providers/samsungHealth.ts&#96;)\\\\\\\\n   - A provider class exists that can read sleep sessions from Samsung Health\\\\\\\\n   - It expects a native module called &#96;SamsungHealth&#96; to be available\\\\\\\\n   - The provider maps Samsung Health data to the unified &#96;SleepSession&#96; format\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n2. **Unified Health Service** (&#96;app/src/lib/health/unifiedService.ts&#96;)\\\\\\\\n   - Automatically selects the best available health provider\\\\\\\\n   - Provides a unified interface for fetching sleep data\\\\\\\\n   - Handles provider priority (Google Fit \u003e Health Connect \u003e Samsung Health)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n3. **Sync Function** (&#96;app/src/lib/sync.ts&#96;)\\\\\\\\n   - &#96;syncHealthData()&#96; function fetches latest sleep from the active provider\\\\\\\\n   - Calls &#96;upsertSleepSessionFromHealth()&#96; to save to Supabase\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n4. **Database Save Function** (&#96;app/src/lib/api.ts&#96;)\\\\\\\\n   - &#96;upsertSleepSessionFromHealth()&#96; saves sleep data to &#96;sleep_sessions&#96; table\\\\\\\\n   - Handles sleep stages, efficiency, heart rate, and other metadata\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n5. **UI Display** (&#96;app/src/screens/SleepScreen.tsx&#96;)\\\\\\\\n   - Shows last night's sleep data\\\\\\\\n   - Displays sleep stages (hypnogram)\\\\\\\\n   - Shows heart rate and body temperature if available\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### ⚠️ What's Missing\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. **Native Module**: The &#96;SamsungHealth&#96; native module is not implemented\\\\\\\\n   - The code expects &#96;NativeModules.SamsungHealth&#96; to exist\\\\\\\\n   - This requires either:\\\\\\\\n     - Samsung Health Partner SDK (official, requires partnership approval)\\\\\\\\n     - OR a custom React Native bridge to Samsung Health APIs\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n2. **Current Workaround**: \\\\\\\\n   - Samsung Health data can be accessed **indirectly** through Google So we never “pull latest” from Health Connect when Supabase is merely stale. |\\\\\\\\n| **Sync not uploading new data** | Same as §2 | If sync doesn’t run or wrongly skips new sessions, Supabase never gets post–23 Jan data, so the app keeps showing 23 Jan. |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Connection chain (files)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- SleepScreen &#96;fetchSleepSessions&#96; → &#96;listSleepSessions(days)&#96; (api.ts) → Supabase; only on empty result → &#96;fetchSessionsFromIntegration(providerId, days)&#96;.  \\\\\\\\n- &#96;fetchLastSleepSession&#96; → integrations first, then Supabase – so “last” can be fresher, but the **sessions list** is still Supabase-first.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### How to fix\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. **Fix sync and “Import latest data”**  \\\\\\\\n   - So that new nights are written to Supabase (§1 and §2). Then “last data” will move forward as sync runs.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n2. **Optional: prefer integration when it’s fresher**  \\\\\\\\n   - Change &#96;fetchSleepSessions&#96; so that when HC (or preferred provider) is connected, it tries **integration first** for the last N days, then **merges** with Supabase (e.g. union by date/session id, prefer HC for overlapping dates).  \\\\\\\\n   - Or: keep Supabase-first but **trigger sync** when the screen loads and the “latest” Supabase session is older than e.g. 2 days, then refetch so we show newly synced data after that run.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n3. **Minimal change**  \\\\\\\\n   - If you only fix §1 and §2, then “Import latest data” and connect will sync, Supabase will get new nights, and the existing “Supabase first” logic will start showing up-to-date data once sync has run.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"2. **Consequence**  \\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":178},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"   - If Supabase has **any** rows (e.g. up to 23 Jan), &#96;fetchSleepSessions(30)&#96; and Settings. Use these conventions for any new screen or when refactoring existing ones so the product remains cohesive.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 1. Layout \u0026 Wrappers\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Wrap primary content in a &#96;ScrollView&#96; with:\\\\\\\\n   - &#96;style={{ backgroundColor: theme.colors.background }}&#96;\\\\\\\\n   - &#96;contentContainerStyle={{ paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingTop: 16, paddingBottom: 140 }}&#96; (bigger bottom padding if a FAB or bottom tabs overlap).\\\\\\\\n2. For list-based screens (e.g., Dashboard &#96;SectionList&#96;), maintain multi-panel layouts but ensure headers and cards use the shared primitives below.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2. Section Headers\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Use &#96;SectionHeader&#96; from &#96;@/components/ui&#96; for every logical grouping (hero, insights, Today, history, etc.).\\\\\\\\n2. When helpful, set &#96;caption&#96; for supporting copy (e.g., “7D • 30D • 365D averages”).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 3. Card Hierarchy\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. **ActionCard** (hero/primary summaries) — typically first block, with prominent icon + headline.\\\\\\\\n2. **Card mode=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"elevated\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"** — default for key panels.\\\\\\\\n3. **Card mode=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"outlined\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"** — informational or fallback/error states.\\\\\\\\n4. Always use &#96;borderRadius: 16&#96; (24 for hero chips if needed) and respect &#96;sectionSpacing&#96; (16) between stacked cards.\\\\\\\\n5. Maintain 8px increments for internal padding/gaps unless the design calls for larger hero spacing.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 6. Typography\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Headings: &#96;variant=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"titleMedium\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; (or &#96;headlineSmall&#96;/&#96;headlineLarge&#96; for hero text). Body copy uses &#96;bodyMedium&#96;; helper text uses &#96;bodySmall&#96;.\\\\\\\\n2. Avoid custom font sizes unless necessary; rely on Paper’s variants for predictability.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 7. Insights Block Pattern\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Each screen with insights should follow: &#96;SectionHeader&#96; → loading card (outlined) → error card (outlined with retry button) → &#96;InsightCard&#96; or an outlined disabled message if insights are off.\\\\\\\\n2. &#96;InsightCard&#96; receives &#96;testID&#96; for QA (&#96;mood-insight-card&#96;, &#96;meds-insight-card&#96;, &#96;dashboard-insight-card&#96;, etc.).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 8. Modals \u0026 Overlays\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Use &#96;Portal&#96; + &#96;Card&#96; or &#96;Modal&#96; with &#96;borderRadius: 16&#96;–&#96;24&#96;, &#96;padding: 16–20&#96;, and &#96;backgroundColor: theme.colors.surface&#96;.\\\\\\\\n2. Backdrops should use &#96;theme.colors.backdrop&#96; or a semi-transparent black (&#96;rgba(0,0,0,0.5)&#96;).\\\\\\\\n3. Buttons inside modals follow the same contained/outlined hierarchy, aligned right for confirm/cancel.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 9. Calendar \u0026 Embedded Cards\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Components like &#96;CalendarCard&#96; that already render their own &#96;Card&#96; should **not** be wrapped in another card. Instead, keep them as direct children within the section.\\\\\\\\n2. If a child component lacks internal framing, wrap it in a card before rendering in the parent (as done for most sections of Dashboard).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 10. Use these conventions for any new screen or when refactoring existing ones so the product remains cohesive.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 1. Layout \u0026 Wrappers\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Wrap primary content in a &#96;ScrollView&#96; with:\\\\\\\\n   - &#96;style={{ backgroundColor: theme.colors.background }}&#96;\\\\\\\\n   - &#96;contentContainerStyle={{ paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingTop: 16, paddingBottom: 140 }}&#96; (bigger bottom padding if a FAB or bottom tabs overlap).\\\\\\\\n2. For list-based screens (e.g., Dashboard &#96;SectionList&#96;), maintain multi-panel layouts but ensure headers and cards use the shared primitives below.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2. Section Headers\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Use &#96;SectionHeader&#96; from &#96;@/components/ui&#96; for every logical grouping (hero, insights, Today, history, etc.).\\\\\\\\n2. Always supply an &#96;icon&#96; that reflects the section (e.g., &#96;calendar-today&#96; for schedules, &#96;lightbulb-on-outline&#96; for insights, &#96;history&#96; for logs).\\\\\\\\n3. When helpful, set &#96;caption&#96; for supporting copy (e.g., “7D • 30D • 365D averages”).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 3. Card Hierarchy\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. **ActionCard** (hero/primary summaries) — typically first block, with prominent icon + headline.\\\\\\\\n2. **Card mode=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"elevated\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"** — default for key panels.\\\\\\\\n3. **Card mode=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"outlined\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"** — informational or fallback/error states.\\\\\\\\n4. Always use &#96;borderRadius: 16&#96; (24 for hero chips if needed) and respect &#96;sectionSpacing&#96; (16) between stacked cards.\\\\\\\\n5. For nested utility sections (forms, tables), place controls inside a single &#96;Card&#96; rather than free-floating views.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 4. Buttons \u0026 Chips\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Primary actions use &#96;mode=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"contained\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;. Secondary actions use &#96;mode=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"outlined\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;. Tertiary/inline actions use &#96;mode=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; (or &#96;contained-tonal&#96; for subtle primary actions).\\\\\\\\n2. When multiple buttons exist in a row, use &#96;View&#96; containers with &#96;columnGap&#96; and avoid ad-hoc &#96;marginRight&#96;. This keeps spacing consistent across screen sizes.\\\\\\\\n3. Chips should be used for quick toggles/status; prefer &#96;mode=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"outlined\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; for neutral states and &#96;mode=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"flat\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"/\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"filled\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; for active ones.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"## UI Theming Contract\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"This document summarizes the shared layout primitives and visual rules we now apply across Dashboard, Mood, Sleep, Meds, Mindfulness, Meditation, Notifications, and Settings. Mood drawings too small in hero section\\\\n\\\\n**Root cause:**\\\\n- File: &#96;c:\\\\\\\\Reclaim\\\\\\\\app\\\\\\\\src\\\\\\\\components\\\\\\\\dashboard\\\\\\\\MoodHero.tsx&#96;\\\\n- Line 74: &#96;centerSize = orbSize * 0.73&#96; (73% of orb size)\\\\n- Lines 71-72: &#96;orbSize&#96; constrained between &#96;ORB_MIN = 140&#96; and &#96;ORB_MAX = 210&#96;\\\\n- The visualization receives &#96;size={centerSize}&#96; (line 151), resulting in a max size of ~153px (210 * 0.73)\\\\n\\\\n**Fix approach:**\\\\n- Increase the multiplier from &#96;0.73&#96; to &#96;0.85-0.90&#96; to make drawings ~20-25% larger\\\\n- Or increase &#96;ORB_MAX&#96; from &#96;210&#96; to &#96;240-250&#96; if keeping the multiplier\\\\n- Symbol: &#96;centerSize&#96; calculation (line 74)\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n### 2. Meds screen 'Due today' lines cut off Taken/Due chips\\\\n\\\\n**Root cause:**\\\\n- File: &#96;c:\\\\\\\\Reclaim\\\\\\\\app\\\\\\\\src\\\\\\\\screens\\\\\\\\MedsScreen.tsx&#96;\\\\n- Lines 798-854: Row layout issue\\\\n- Line 822: Middle &#96;View&#96; has &#96;flex: 1&#96; (can shrink)\\\\n- Line 823: Med name text with &#96;numberOfLines={1}&#96; can push content\\\\n- Line 827: Chip is inside the &#96;flex: 1&#96; View, so it can be clipped\\\\n- Line 855: Right button container lacks &#96;flexShrink: 0&#96;, allowing compression\\\\n\\\\n**Fix approach:**\\\\n- Add &#96;flexShrink: 0&#96; to the right button container (line 855)\\\\n- Wrap med name and Chip in separate containers, or use &#96;flexWrap: 'wrap'&#96; on the middle View\\\\n- Ensure Chip has &#96;flexShrink: 0&#96; or move it outside the &#96;flex: 1&#96; container\\\\n- Symbols: &#96;dueTodayItems.map&#96; row structure (lines 798-879)\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n### 3. Meds screen hero explanation text truncates with ellipses\\\\n\\\\n**Root cause:**\\\\n- File: &#96;c:\\\\\\\\Reclaim\\\\\\\\app\\\\\\\\src\\\\\\\\components\\\\\\\\dashboard\\\\\\\\MedsHero.tsx&#96;\\\\n- Lines 281-295: Context line text layout\\\\n- Line 289: &#96;maxWidth: '45%'&#96; combined with &#96;flex: 1&#96; and &#96;numberOfLines={2}&#96;\\\\n- Line 256: Chip container has &#96;maxWidth: '52%'&#96; and &#96;flexShrink: 0&#96;\\\\n- When chips are wide, the text gets squeezed below 45% and truncates\\\\n\\\\n**Fix approach:**\\\\n- Remove &#96;maxWidth: '45%'&#96; constraint, keep &#96;flex: 1&#96; with &#96;numberOfLines={2}&#96;\\\\n- Or increase &#96;maxWidth&#96; to &#96;'50%'&#96; or &#96;'55%'&#96;\\\\n- Reduce chip container &#96;maxWidth&#96; from &#96;'52%'&#96; to &#96;'48%'&#96; to give more space to text\\\\n- Symbol: Context line &#96;Text&#96; component (lines 282-294)\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n### 4. Dashboard has too large gap between hero and first card\\\\n\\\\n**Root cause:**\\\\n- File: &#96;c:\\\\\\\\Reclaim\\\\\\\\app\\\\\\\\src\\\\\\\\screens\\\\\\\\Dashboard.tsx&#96;\\\\n- Line 1649: &#96;LifecycleHero&#96; rendered\\\\n- Line 1650: &#96;View&#96; with &#96;paddingTop: 16&#96;\\\\n- File: &#96;c:\\\\\\\\Reclaim\\\\\\\\app\\\\\\\\src\\\\\\\\components\\\\\\\\dashboard\\\\\\\\LifecycleHero.tsx&#96;\\\\n- Line 95: &#96;PADDING_BOTTOM = 16&#96;\\\\n- Total gap = 32px (16 + 16), should be ~16px\\\\n\\\\n**Fix approach:**\\\\n- Reduce &#96;paddingTop&#96; from &#96;16&#96; to &#96;0&#96; or &#96;4&#96; (line 1650 in Dashboard.tsx)\\\\n- Or reduce &#96;PADDING_BOTTOM&#96; from &#96;16&#96; to &#96;8&#96; in LifecycleHero.tsx (line 95)\\\\n- Prefer reducing &#96;paddingTop&#96; to keep hero spacing consistent\\\\n- Symbol: &#96;paddingTop: 16&#96; (Dashboard.tsx line 1650)\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Cross-device/responsive risks\\\\n\\\\n1. Mood drawings: Increasing size may overflow on small screens (\u003c 360px width). Add a min/max clamp or responsive scaling.\\\\n2. Meds chips: Long medication names + dose strings can still overflow. Test with names like \\\\\\\"Sertraline Hydrochloride Extended Release\\\\\\\" + \\\\\\\"100mg\\\\\\\".\\\\n3. SessionTemplate; days: number[] }[] {\\\\\\\\n  // Determine dominant goal\\\\\\\\n  const goalEntries = Object.entries(goals).filter(([, w]) =\u003e w \u0026\u0026 w \u003e 0);\\\\\\\\n  if (goalEntries.length === 0) {\\\\\\\\n    goalEntries.push(['build_muscle', 0.5]);\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n  goalEntries.sort(([, a], [, b]) =\u003e b - a);\\\\\\\\n  const dominantGoal = goalEntries[0][0];\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // 2 days: Full body A/B\\\\\\\\n  if (daysPerWeek === 2) {\\\\\\\\n    return [\\\\\\\\n      { template: 'full_body' as SessionTemplate, days: [1, 4] }, // Mon, Thu\\\\\\\\n    ];\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // 3 days: Full body or Upper/Lower or PPL depending on goals\\\\\\\\n  if (daysPerWeek === 3) {\\\\\\\\n    if (dominantGoal === 'build_strength') {\\\\\\\\n      // Full body for strength\\\\\\\\n      return [{ template: 'full_body' as SessionTemplate, days: [1, 3, 5] }]; // Mon, Wed, Fri\\\\\\\\n    } else if (dominantGoal === 'lose_fat' || dominantGoal === 'get_fitter') {\\\\\\\\n      // Upper/Lower for conditioning\\\\\\\\n      return [\\\\\\\\n        { template: 'upper' as SessionTemplate, days: [1, 5] }, // Mon, Fri\\\\\\\\n        { template: 'lower' as SessionTemplate, days: [3] }, // Wed\\\\\\\\n      ];\\\\\\\\n    } else {\\\\\\\\n      // PPL for hypertrophy\\\\\\\\n      return [\\\\\\\\n        { template: 'push' as SessionTemplate, days: [1] }, // Mon\\\\\\\\n        { template: 'pull' as SessionTemplate, days: [3] }, // Wed\\\\\\\\n        { template: 'legs' as SessionTemplate, days: [5] }, // Fri\\\\\\\\n      ];\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // 4 days: Upper/Lower split\\\\\\\\n  if (daysPerWeek === 4) {\\\\\\\\n    return [\\\\\\\\n      { template: 'upper' as SessionTemplate, days: [1, 4] }, // Mon, Thu\\\\\\\\n      { template: 'lower' as SessionTemplate, days: [2, 5] }, // Tue, Fri\\\\\\\\n    ];\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // 5+ days: PPL + accessories\\\\\\\\n  return [\\\\\\\\n    { template: 'push' as SessionTemplate, days: [1, 4] }, // Mon, Thu\\\\\\\\n    { template: 'pull' as SessionTemplate, days: [2, 5] }, // Tue, Fri\\\\\\\\n    { template: 'legs' as SessionTemplate, days: [3] }, // Wed\\\\\\\\n    { template: 'conditioning' as SessionTemplate, days: [6] }, // Sat (optional)\\\\\\\\n  ];\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n/**\\\\\\\\n * Generate routine template ID for training session\\\\\\\\n */\\\\\\\\nexport function getTrainingRoutineTemplateId(template: SessionTemplate): string {\\\\\\\\n  return &#96;training_${template}&#96;;\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n/**\\\\\\\\n * Create routine suggestions for the week based on training profile\\\\\\\\n */\\\\\\\\nexport async function generateWeeklyTrainingPlan(profile: TrainingProfileRow): Promise\u003cvoid\u003e {\\\\\\\\n  const split = determineWeeklySplit(profile.days_per_week, profile.goals);\\\\\\\\n  const today = new Date();\\\\\\\\n  const currentWeekStart = new Date(today);\\\\\\\\n  currentWeekStart.setDate(today.getDate() - today.getDay() + 1); // Monday\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // Get time window\\\\\\\\n  const timeWindow = profile.preferred_time_window || {};\\\\\\\\n  const isMorning = timeWindow.morning || false;\\\\\\\\n  const isEvening = timeWindow.evening || false;\\\\\\\\n  const startRange = timeWindow.startRange || (isMorning ? 6 : 17);\\\\\\\\n  const endRange = timeWindow.endRange || (isMorning ? 10 : 21);\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // Generate suggestions for each day in the split\\\\\\\\n  for (const { template, days } of split) {\\\\\\\\n    for (const dayOffset of days) {\\\\\\\\n      const targetDate = new Date(currentWeekStart);\\\\\\\\n      targetDate.setDate(currentWeekStart.getDate() + dayOffset - 1);\\\\\\\\n      const dateStr = getLocalDateKey(targetDate);\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n      // Calculate suggested time (middle of window)\\\\\\\\n      const suggestedHour = Math.floor((startRange + endRange) / 2);\\\\\\\\n      const suggestedMinute = ((startRange + endRange) / 2) % 1 === 0 ? 0 : 30;\\\\\\\\n      const suggestedStart = new Date(targetDate);\\\\\\\\n      suggestedStart.setHours(suggestedHour, suggestedMinute, 0, 0);\\\\\\\\n      const suggestedEnd = new Date(suggestedStart);\\\\\\\\n      suggestedEnd.setMinutes(suggestedEnd.getMinutes() + 60); // 60 min session\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n      const templateId = getTrainingRoutineTemplateId(template);\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n      await upsertRoutineSuggestionRemote({\\\\\\\\n        routine_template_id: templateId,\\\\\\\\n        date: dateStr,\\\\\\\\n        state: 'suggested' as RoutineSuggestionState,\\\\\\\\n        suggested_start_ts: suggestedStart.toISOString(),\\\\\\\\n        suggested_end_ts: suggestedEnd.toISOString(),\\\\\\\\n        reason: &#96;Scheduled ${template} session based on your training plan.&#96;,\\\\\\\\n      });\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n/**\\\\\\\\n * Find next available slot if conflict exists\\\\\\\\n */\\\\\\\\nexport function findNextAvailableSlot(\\\\\\\\n  preferredDate: Date,\\\\\\\\n  preferredStart: Date,\\\\\\\\n  preferredEnd: Date,\\\\\\\\n): { start: Date; end: Date } {\\\\\\\\n  // Try same day, 1 hour 6 : 17);\\\\n  const endRange = timeWindow.endRange || (timeWindow.morning ? 10 : 21);\\\\n  const suggestedHour = Math.floor((startRange + endRange) / 2);\\\\n  \\\\n  for (const day of programDays) {\\\\n    const date = new Date(day.date);\\\\n    const suggestedStart = new Date(date);\\\\n    suggestedStart.setHours(suggestedHour, 0, 0, 0);\\\\n    \\\\n    await upsertRoutineSuggestionRemote({\\\\n      routine_template_id: &#96;training_${day.template_key}&#96;,\\\\n      date: day.date,\\\\n      state: 'suggested',\\\\n      suggested_start_ts: suggestedStart.toISOString(),\\\\n      suggested_end_ts: new Date(suggestedStart.getTime() + 60*60*1000).toISOString(),\\\\n      reason: &#96;Scheduled ${day.label} from your program.&#96;,\\\\n    });\\\\n  }\\\\n}\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n#### Fix 2: Improve deduplication in Dashboard\\\\n\\\\nProblem: Dashboard shows both routine suggestions and program day fallback.\\\\n\\\\nSolution: Check both accepted and suggested routines:\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\n// Dashboard.tsx line 1270 - IMPROVE:\\\\nconst hasTrainingRoutine = acceptedRoutineItems.some((r) =\u003e r.templateId.startsWith('training_')) ||\\\\n  routineSuggestions.some((r) =\u003e r.template.id.startsWith('training_'));\\\\n\\\\nif (todayProgramDay \u0026\u0026 !hasTrainingRoutine) {\\\\n  // Only show fallback if NO training routine exists (accepted OR suggested)\\\\n}\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n#### Fix 3: Align time calculations\\\\n\\\\nProblem: Different time calculation methods cause hour shifts.\\\\n\\\\nSolution: Use consistent time calculation:\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\nfunction calculateSuggestedTime(timeWindow: any): Date {\\\\n  const isMorning = timeWindow.morning ?? (isMorning ? 6 : 17);\\\\n  const endRange = timeWindow.endRange ?? (isMorning ? 10 : 21);\\\\n  const suggestedHour = Math.floor((startRange + endRange) / 2);\\\\n  const suggestedMinute = ((startRange + endRange) / 2) % 1 === 0 ? 0 : 30;\\\\n  \\\\n  const date = new Date();\\\\n  date.setHours(suggestedHour, suggestedMinute, 0, 0);\\\\n  return date;\\\\n}\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n#### Fix 4: Remove conflicting logic\\\\n\\\\nProblem: &#96;determineWeeklySplit()&#96; conflicts with &#96;determineSplit()&#96;.\\\\n\\\\nSolution: Remove &#96;determineWeeklySplit()&#96; and use program days exclusively:\\\\n- Delete &#96;generateWeeklyTrainingPlan()&#96; function\\\\n- Remove &#96;determineWeeklySplit()&#96; function\\\\n- Use &#96;getProgramDays()&#96; query results to generate routine suggestions\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n### Part 4: Medication catalogue expansion recommendations\\\\n\\\\n#### Option A: Manual curation (recommended for MVP)\\\\n\\\\nPros:\\\\n- Full control over content quality\\\\n- No API dependencies\\\\n- Faster to implement\\\\n- Better legal/clinical safety\\\\n\\\\nCons:\\\\n- Requires manual updates\\\\n- Limited scalability\\\\n\\\\nImplementation:\\\\n1. Migration path: &#96;loadMedCatalog()&#96; checks version, falls back\\\\n\\\\n#### Option B: API integration (long-term)\\\\n\\\\nCandidates:\\\\n1. OpenFDA: Free, safety-focused, less comprehensive\\\\n\\\\nImplementation:\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\n// Hybrid approach: Static catalog + API fallback\\\\nasync function findMedCatalogItem(name: string): Promise\u003cMedCatalogItem | null\u003e {\\\\n  // 1. API fallback (slower, requires network)\\\\n  if (await isOnline()) {\\\\n    const apiMatch = await searchRxNormAPI(name);\\\\n    if (apiMatch) {\\\\n      // Cache in local catalog for future use\\\\n      await cacheMedCatalogItem(apiMatch);\\\\n      return apiMatch;\\\\n    }\\\\n  }\\\\n  \\\\n  return null;\\\\n}\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n#### Option C: Hybrid approach (recommended)\\\\n\\\\n1. Static catalog: Core 50-100 most common medications\\\\n2. API fallback: For unknown medications\\\\n3. User contributions: Allow users to suggest additions (moderated)\\\\n4. Auto-caching: Cache API results in static catalog for future releases\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n### Part 5: DSM-5 inclusion — legal/clinical safety analysis\\\\n\\\\n#### Current state\\\\n- No DSM-5 diagnostic content found in codebase\\\\n- App focuses on medication tracking and adherence\\\\n- Educational content only (mechanisms, effects)\\\\n\\\\n#### Legal risks of including DSM-5\\\\n\\\\n1. Versioning: Track catalog version, allow migration\\\\n4. Audit trail: Log when catalog items are viewed/used\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n### Summary\\\\n\\\\nWorkout duplication:\\\\n- Root cause: Two independent scheduling systems\\\\n- Fix: Unify on program days, remove &#96;generateWeeklyTrainingPlan()&#96;\\\\n- Time issue: Standardize time calculation logic\\\\n\\\\nMedication catalogue:\\\\n- Current: Static JSON, 12 medications\\\\n- Recommendation: Hybrid (static core + API fallback)\\\\n- Expansion: Manual curation → 50 medications → API integration\\\\n\\\\nDSM-5:\\\\n- Risk: High (copyright, liability, medical advice)\\\\n- Recommendation: Do not include directly\\\\n- Alternative: Symptom categories, ICD-10 codes, educational framing\\\\n\\\\nNext steps:\\\\n1. _**Agent (default)**_

Absolutely doable. I reviewed the relevant modules and mapped each issue to likely root cause(s), best-practice fix, and regression risk.

No code changes below — this is diagnosis + implementation blueprint only.

## Root Causes And Exact Fixes

- **Google Fit disconnects after close/reopen**
  - **Why it happens:** connection status is repeatedly reconciled from runtime permission checks in `lib/health/integrations.ts`; transient false returns can flip provider to disconnected. Sync orchestration in `sync/SyncCoordinator.ts` currently trusts stored state heavily (`forceRuntimeConnectedProviders = false`), so once state flips, imports can behave like provider is gone.
  - **Best fix:** move to a provider-state model (`connected`, `verifying`, `degraded`, `disconnected`) with hysteresis (do not mark disconnected on one failed probe); require repeated failures over a window before demotion. Also run a warm-up permission probe on foreground before declaring disconnected.
  - **Regression risk:** true revocations may take slightly longer to show. Mitigate by surfacing `verifying`/`needs attention` rather than instant hard disconnect.

- **Integrations import is slow, ends with “needs attention,” and sometimes says no provider diagnostics**
  - **Why it happens:** `processImport` in `screens/IntegrationsScreen.tsx` wraps sync in a fixed timeout; when timeout hits, `syncResult` can be null and per-provider diagnostics map is missing, producing “No provider diagnostics were returned.”
  - **Best fix:** split import into 2 phases: preflight diagnostics (always available) + async sync job (progress + result polling). Keep provider diagnostics populated even if sync times out/fails.
  - **Regression risk:** UI complexity increases. Mitigate with one canonical `ImportRunResult` type used by Sleep and Integrations screens.

- **Sleep history sometimes shows none until reconnect/import**
  - **Why it happens:** `SleepScreen` query flow can render empty states while foreground invalidation/refetch races with integration reconciliation and sync; it also falls back between Supabase/provider data in ways that can briefly return empty.
  - **Best fix:** make local DB/Supabase the UI source-of-truth and run provider sync in background; use `keepPreviousData` + explicit `isInitialLoading` guard so you don’t render “empty” until first fetch resolves.
  - **Regression risk:** stale rows could persist longer onscreen. Mitigate with refresh badge (“Last updated X min ago”) and deterministic refresh lifecycle.

- **Mood drawings still too small**
  - **Why it happens:** `centerSize` in `components/dashboard/MoodHero.tsx` is constrained (`orbSize * 0.73`), which keeps visual payload small.
  - **Best fix:** increase visual center ratio (e.g., 0.85–0.9) and rebalance overlay spacing/chip anchor points accordingly.
  - **Regression risk:** overflow on compact devices. Mitigate with width-based clamp profiles.

- **Dashboard resyncs too often**
  - **Why it happens:** dashboard-level AppState listener in `screens/Dashboard.tsx` triggers `runHealthSync` on active transitions with short cooldown.
  - **Best fix:** centralize sync cadence in `SyncCoordinator` only; screen should observe shared sync state, not own foreground sync loop.
  - **Regression risk:** slower refresh after returning to app. Mitigate with manual pull-to-refresh and stale-age threshold.

- **Meds “Due today” row cuts off chips/buttons**
  - **Why it happens:** row uses `flex:1` text/chip block plus action buttons without strict shrink constraints in `screens/MedsScreen.tsx`.
  - **Best fix:** switch to a 2-column responsive row contract: left content wraps, right action rail fixed min width; chip on separate line with no clipping.
  - **Regression risk:** taller rows. Mitigate with consistent row height tiers and test with long med names.

- **Duplicate notifications when opening app**
  - **Why it happens:** `useNotifications` currently reconciles immediately and also schedules deferred reconciles plus foreground reconcile, so multiple reconciliation triggers cluster together.
  - **Best fix:** replace timer-based deferred reconciles with event-based readiness reconcile (data ready/auth ready), and enforce one reconciliation pipeline token at a time.
  - **Regression risk:** if readiness signal fails, some reminders may appear later. Mitigate with fallback watchdog reconcile after longer timeout.

- **Do notifications still fire when app is closed?**
  - **Current architecture:** yes, because they’re scheduled via native OS (`expo-notifications`) in `NotificationScheduler`; OS should fire even when app is closed.
  - **Caveat:** OEM battery policies (some Android vendors) can delay/drop behavior.
  - **Best fix:** add device-level verification suite + diagnostics event logging (scheduled count, fired count, late-delivery delta) to prove behavior in production.
  - **Regression risk:** none functionally; mostly observability work.

- **Meds hero explanation text gets ellipsized**
  - **Why it happens:** constrained width and `numberOfLines` in `components/dashboard/MedsHero.tsx` force truncation.
  - **Best fix:** remove hard width cap for that text block and allow natural wrap (or dynamic width split based on chip content width).
  - **Regression risk:** text can push chips on very small screens. Mitigate with responsive breakpoint rule.

- **Large gap between dashboard hero and first card**
  - **Why it happens:** combined bottom padding from hero and top padding from next container (`LifecycleHero` + `Dashboard`).
  - **Best fix:** normalize section spacing tokens and ensure only one source of vertical gap between adjacent blocks.
  - **Regression risk:** spacing may feel cramped on tablets. Mitigate with size-class spacing scale.

- **Sleep score missing most of the time**
  - **Why it happens:** score ring in `SleepScreen` uses provider `quality` only for “Score” metric; many providers don’t populate quality consistently.
  - **Best fix:** define a computed composite score fallback (duration vs target + efficiency + stage coverage), persist derived score, and label as “Estimated” when provider score absent.
  - **Regression risk:** users may compare old/new score semantics. Mitigate with migration note and tooltip.

- **Stale data flashes then suddenly updates**
  - **Why it happens:** broad invalidation + immediate refetch patterns across screens; UI renders stale snapshot then swaps to new data with no transition contract.
  - **Best fix:** adopt a screen data lifecycle contract: `bootstrap -> stable snapshot -> background refresh -> subtle delta update`, not hard swap. Use cache retention and optimistic derived view models.
  - **Regression risk:** perceived slower updates. Mitigate with “Refreshing…” micro-state.

- **Phone lock/unlock showing empty history then appearing**
  - **Why it happens:** same race as above on app active in `SleepScreen` (invalidate + refetch + render order).
  - **Best fix:** do not show empty state while active refetch is pending unless first load truly completed with zero data.
  - **Regression risk:** none meaningful; UX improvement.

- **Dashboard hypnogram inconsistent vs full sleep window**
  - **Why it happens:** merged sessions can have full-night start/end but partial stage timelines; renderer (`components/dashboard/DashboardSleep.tsx`) doesn’t enforce stage coverage validity.
  - **Best fix:** add stage coverage quality gate:
    - if stage coverage >= threshold (e.g., 60%), render hypnogram;
    - else show “partial stage data” indicator and fallback visualization.
  - **Regression risk:** fewer hypnograms shown initially. Mitigate with transparent messaging instead of misleading chart.

- **Workout plans duplicate / extra “Push” appears earlier**
  - **Why it happens:** dual scheduling paths conflict:
    - generated weekly suggestions from `lib/training/scheduler.ts` (`generateWeeklyTrainingPlan`)
    - dashboard fallback program-day training insertion in `screens/Dashboard.tsx`
    - different time logic between systems.
  - **Best fix:** single source of truth for training scheduling (program days). Decommission or refactor weekly generator to consume program days, and remove fallback insertion when any training suggestion already exists (accepted or suggested).
  - **Regression risk:** users relying on old auto-suggestion behavior may see schedule shift. Mitigate with one-time migration + clear in-app note.

## Medication Catalogue Expansion (And DSM-5 Question)

- **Current state:** static JSON catalog in `data/medCatalog.v1.json` loaded by `lib/medCatalog.ts`.
- **Best architecture:** hybrid model
  - curated offline core catalog (high-confidence, clinically reviewed),
  - enrichment layer from free/public APIs for unknown meds,
  - local cache + moderation pipeline for promoted entries.
- **Good free sources:**
  - RxNorm (normalization and identifiers),
  - DailyMed SPL (label text, warnings),
  - openFDA labels (safety/labeling metadata).
- **DSM-5 inclusion recommendation:** do **not** embed DSM-5 criteria text directly (copyright + self-diagnosis risk).  
  Prefer symptom-domain education, ICD-10/clinical category mapping, and strict “not diagnostic advice” framing.

## Other Integrations To Make It Feel Premium (Accuracy + Retention)

- **High impact health accuracy:** Oura, Fitbit, Garmin, WHOOP, Polar, Withings sleep/HRV.
- **Medication adherence moat:** pharmacy refill integrations, smart pillbox/smart-cap devices, refill prediction + depletion alerts.
- **Behavior retention:** coach messaging loop, weekly “insight digest,” adaptive nudges by chronotype/adherence pattern.
- **Clinical credibility:** clinician shareable summary PDF/FHIR export, visit prep notes, adherence + symptom timeline.
- **Lifestyle context:** nutrition (Cronometer/MyFitnessPal), stress (HRV wearable), menstrual cycle context, calendar + commute stress windows.
- **Long-term differentiation:** relapse-risk early warning model (privacy-safe), habit recovery scoring, intervention A/B personalization.

## Execution Order I Recommend (To Avoid Regressions)

- **Phase 1 (stability first):** sync state machine, diagnostics contract, duplicate notification reconciliation fix.
- **Phase 2 (data UX):** loading lifecycle contract, sleep history/score/hypnogram reliability.
- **Phase 3 (layout polish):** mood hero scale, meds row clipping, hero text wrap, dashboard spacing.
- **Phase 4 (training):** unify scheduling source-of-truth + dedupe migration.
- **Phase 5 (catalogue):** expand curated meds + API enrichment pipeline + compliance framing.

If you want, I can turn this into a concrete implementation checklist with exact file-by-file changes and a test matrix before we touch code.

_**Agent (default)**_

Yes — materially better, not just “different.”

- **More reliable behavior:** fewer race conditions (sync, notifications, screen refetch loops), so less “empty then suddenly filled” UI and fewer duplicate notifications.
- **Cleaner architecture:** one source of truth for training scheduling and sync orchestration removes conflicting code paths.
- **Higher maintainability:** less hidden coupling between screens; easier to reason about and debug.
- **Better observability:** standardized provider diagnostics means faster root-cause detection when imports fail.
- **Better UX consistency:** stable loading lifecycle and responsive layout fixes remove clipping/truncation/janky transitions.
- **Safer future growth:** med catalog/API expansion on a structured pipeline avoids brittle one-off additions.

Only caveat: it increases **initial implementation complexity**, so it should be rolled out in phases with regression tests. If done that way, it absolutely makes the codebase better long-term.

2-file chunk done and stopped.

### Files changed

1. `app/src/lib/health/integrations.ts`
- Added transient-disconnect protection in `reconcileStoredIntegrationStatuses()`:
  - single failed runtime probe no longer immediately flips a previously connected provider to disconnected.
  - requires consecutive failed probes before disconnecting (`DISCONNECT_CONFIRMATION_FAILURES = 2`).
- Added debug logging for ignored transient misses.
- This specifically targets the “Google Fit randomly disconnects after reopen” behavior.

2. `app/src/screens/Dashboard.tsx`
- Hardened training fallback dedupe logic:
  - `hasTrainingRoutineToday` now uses **local date parsing** (`formatLocalDateYYYYMMDD(new Date(startISO))`) instead of raw ISO slicing.
  - Also treats training suggestions with missing `startISO` as existing (to avoid fallback duplicates).
- This targets duplicate workout entries / shifted-time fallback artifacts.

### Validation
- Lint check run on both files: **no errors**.

If you approve, next 2-file chunk should be:
- `app/src/screens/SleepScreen.tsx`
- `app/src/components/dashboard/DashboardSleep.tsx`  
to finish `sleep-score-hypnogram` (score fallback + hypnogram consistency).

_**Agent (default)**_

Readiness advice based on your current repo and checks:

- `typecheck` now passes (I fixed 3 blockers, including one in `DashboardSleep` and the adherence typing path in `api`).
- `lint` still reports 9 errors (duplicate imports in other files) + warnings.  
  - Not always a runtime blocker, but **is** a quality/CI blocker if your pipeline enforces lint.

## Should you send to WhatsApp testers now?

Yes — but as a **closed alpha**, not broad beta/public yet.

- Start with **10–20 trusted testers** for 3–5 days.
- Focus on crash/stability + core flows (integrations, sleep, meds, notifications).
- Keep production users out until crash-free and no P0/P1 regressions.

## Fast Runtime QA Checklist (do this before sharing link)

Use this as a pass/fail smoke test on at least 2 real devices.

- **App lifecycle**
  - Fresh install -> login -> reopen app 5–10 times from background/locked state.
  - Pass: no crash, no major blank flashes, no stale-to-new jank on main cards.

- **Integrations**
  - Connect Google Fit / Health Connect, run import.
  - Pass: import completes without generic “no diagnostics” message; provider state survives app restart.

- **Sleep**
  - Open sleep after cold start and after unlock.
  - Pass: history loads reliably, score shows fallback when provider quality missing, hypnogram only shown when coverage is sufficient (otherwise clear “partial data hidden” message).

- **Dashboard**
  - Open/close dashboard repeatedly.
  - Pass: no repeated heavy resync behavior each open, spacing looks correct, sleep summary/hypnogram consistent.

- **Meds**
  - In “Today” rows, verify `Taken`/`Due` chips on small/large text settings.
  - Pass: chips and buttons not cut off.
  - Hero text should not be ellipsized unexpectedly.

- **Mood**
  - Hero center drawing should appear visibly larger and proportionate.

- **Notifications**
  - Schedule a near-term reminder, close app, wait.
  - Pass: exactly one notification delivered, reopening app doesn’t create duplicate notifications.

## Best way to launch this alpha (your setup)

You already have EAS profiles (`preview`, `preview-ios`), so use them.

- **Android closed alpha (fastest for WhatsApp groups):**
  - Build internal APK: `eas build -p android --profile preview`
  - Share install link in WhatsApp.
- **iOS closed alpha:**
  - Use TestFlight (recommended for non-technical testers): `eas build -p ios --profile production-ios` then submit.

For quick JS-only fixes during alpha:
- Push OTA to preview channel: `eas update --channel preview --message "alpha hotfix ..."`

## My recommendation

- Do a 45–60 min smoke run with the checklist above.
- If it passes: ship to a small WhatsApp alpha group **today**.
- Track daily:
  - crash-free sessions
  - top 5 Sentry issues
  - notification duplicates
  - integration reconnect/import reliability

If you want, I can next:
1) clean the remaining lint errors fast, and  
2) give you a copy-paste tester message template for WhatsApp (with exact bug-report format).

---

_**Agent (default)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Providing architecture advice**</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

Yes — for alpha testing, that is a very strong idea.

It will be **much easier to fix issues** if reports are created right where the tester sees the problem, instead of only through `Settings -> Report Bug`.

## Best way to do it (so it stays clean)

Don’t show a permanent bug button on every card for normal users.  
Use an **Alpha Feedback Mode**:

- Toggle in settings: `Enable tester feedback mode`
- When enabled: small bug icon on cards/screens
- Tap icon -> report modal opens with prefilled context
- Auto-captures card/screen context + screenshot
- Sends to Supabase (and optional Sentry link)

That gives precision without cluttering your UI for everyone.

## What the report should capture automatically

- app/build info (`version`, `build`, `channel`)
- user id (or tester id), timestamp
- route/screen name + component/card id
- current visible state snapshot (structured JSON, not raw entire app state)
- key data freshness info (loading/fetching/stale flags)
- screenshot (card or full screen)
- tester note (`color off`, `text wrong`, `same message repeated`, etc.)
- optional category + severity

For your “message is the same” case, also include:
- `message_id/hash`
- `context_hash` (inputs used to generate it)
So you can detect repetition bugs quickly.

## Important guardrails

- **Privacy:** whitelist only needed fields (no full health payload dumps)
- **Rate limit:** prevent spam submits
- **Dedup:** hash report context so duplicates group together
- **Offline queue:** store and retry if tester has no network
- **Alpha-only flag:** keep this hidden in production builds

## Recommendation

Yes, do this before wider beta/public.  
It will improve bug quality dramatically and speed up fixes.

If you want, next I can give you a concrete implementation blueprint (tables, payload schema, and rollout order) before we write code.

+## What's Already Wired
 
-Just install &#96;@sentry/react-native&#96; and set the DSN to enable it.

+---

+| Current init logic       | &#96;app/src/lib/sentry.ts&#96;                                |

-// Simple adherence calc: taken / scheduled
+// Simple adherence calc: taken / scheduled (legacy - uses log count as denominator)
 export function computeAdherence(logs: MedDoseLog[]) {
   const scheduled = logs.length;
   const taken = logs.filter((l) =&gt; l.status === 'taken').length;
@@ -1302,6 +1302,67 @@ export function computeAdherence(logs: MedDoseLog[]) {
   return { scheduled, taken, pct };
 }
 
+/**
+ * Count expected dose slots for a schedule within a date range (inclusive).
+ * Used for schedule-based adherence: expected = sum over meds, taken = from logs.
+ */
+export function countExpectedDosesInRange(
+  schedule: { times: string[]; days: number[] } | undefined,
+  start: Date,
+  end: Date
+): number {
+  if (!schedule?.times?.length || !schedule?.days?.length) return 0;
+  let count = 0;
+  const cursor = new Date(start);
+  cursor.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
+  const endDay = new Date(end);
+  endDay.setHours(23, 59, 59, 999);
+  while (cursor &lt;= endDay) {
+    const policyDay = jsDayToPolicy(cursor.getDay());
+    if (schedule.days.includes(policyDay)) {
+      count += schedule.times.length;
+    }
+    cursor.setDate(cursor.getDate() + 1);
+  }
+  return count;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Schedule-based adherence: expected = doses from med schedules in last N days,
+ * taken = logs with status 'taken'. Correctly shows low adherence when user misses doses.
+ */
+export function computeAdherenceFromSchedule(
+  logs: MedDoseLog[],
+  meds: Array&lt;{ id?: string; schedule?: { times: string[]; days: number[] } | undefined }&gt;,
+  days = 7
+): { scheduled: number; taken: number; pct: number } {
+  const end = new Date();
+  end.setHours(23, 59, 59, 999);
+  const start = new Date(end);
+  start.setDate(end.getDate() - (days - 1));
+  start.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
+
+  let expected = 0;
+  for (const med of meds) {
+    if (med.schedule &amp;&amp; med.id) {
+      expected += countExpectedDosesInRange(med.schedule as { times: string[]; days: number[] }, start, end);
+    }
+  }
+
+  const windowStart = start.getTime();
+  const windowEnd = end.getTime();
+  const taken = logs.filter((l) =&gt; {
+    if (l.status !== 'taken') return false;
+    const t = l.taken_at ?? (l as any).scheduled_for ?? (l as any).created_at;
+    if (!t) return false;
+    const ms = new Date(t).getTime();
+    return ms &gt;= windowStart &amp;&amp; ms &lt;= windowEnd;
+  }).length;
+
+  const pct = expected &gt; 0 ? Math.round((taken / expected) * 100) : 0;
+  return { scheduled: expected, taken, pct };
+}
+

 // Medication events (normalized, remote first)
 // -------------------------

  * Used by TrainingSessionView and notification handler to schedule TRAINING_REST and TRAINING_SET
  * with full payloads for SET_DONE/NEXT_SET execution without opening the app.
  */
-import { setIntent } from './NotificationIntentStore';
+import { setIntent, clearIntentsByPrefix } from './NotificationIntentStore';
 import { reconcileNotifications } from './NotificationScheduler';
 import { logger } from '@/lib/logger';
 
+/**
+ * Clear stale training intents when no session is in progress.
+ * Call on app foreground to prevent "Rest complete" / "Session started" notifications
+ * after user abandoned a session (force-closed, navigated away).
+ * On listTrainingSessions failure (e.g. offline), clears intents as safe default.
+ */
+export async function clearStaleTrainingIntentsIfNoActiveSession(): Promise&lt;void&gt; {
+  let inProgress = false;
+  try {
+    const { listTrainingSessions } = await import('@/lib/api');
+    const timeoutPromise = new Promise&lt;never&gt;((_, reject) =&gt;
+      setTimeout(() =&gt; reject(new Error('listTrainingSessions timeout')), 5000)
+    );
+    const sessions = await Promise.race([listTrainingSessions(10), timeoutPromise]);
+    inProgress = (sessions ?? []).some((s: any) =&gt; s?.started_at &amp;&amp; !s?.ended_at);
+  } catch (e) {
+    logger.debug('[TRAINING_NOTIF] listTrainingSessions failed, clearing intents (safe default):', (e as Error)?.message);
+  }
+  if (inProgress) return;
+
+  try {
+    await clearIntentsByPrefix('training_rest:');
+    await clearIntentsByPrefix('training_set:');
+    await clearIntentsByPrefix('training_first:');
+    logger.debug('[TRAINING_NOTIF] Cleared stale intents (no active session)');
+  } catch (e) {
+    logger.debug('[TRAINING_NOTIF] clearIntents failed:', (e as Error)?.message);
+  }
+}

   sessionItemId: string;
   exerciseId: string;

+function buildSyncFallbackResult(

+  options: { timedOut: boolean; message: string },
+): HealthSyncResult {
+  const sleepProviders: Record&lt;SleepProviderDebugKey, any&gt; = {
+    health_connect: {
+      provider: 'health_connect',
+      connected: false,
+      available: false,
+      hasPermissions: false,

+      sessionsRead: 0,

+      connected: false,
+      available: false,
+      hasPermissions: false,
+      windowDays: 0,
+      sessionsRead: 0,
+      writeAttempts: 0,
+      writeSuccesses: 0,
+      skippedExisting: 0,
+      skippedInvalid: 0,
+      skippedMissingTimes: 0,
+      note: options.timedOut ? 'sync_pending' : 'sync_error',
+      errors: [options.message],
+    },
+    apple_healthkit: {
+      provider: 'apple_healthkit',
+      connected: false,
+      available: false,
+      hasPermissions: false,
+      windowDays: 0,
+      sessionsRead: 0,
+      writeAttempts: 0,
+      writeSuccesses: 0,
+      skippedExisting: 0,

+      errors: [options.message],

+    samsung_health: {
+      provider: 'samsung_health',
+      connected: false,
+      available: false,
+      hasPermissions: false,
+      windowDays: 0,
+      sessionsRead: 0,
+      writeAttempts: 0,
+      writeSuccesses: 0,
+      skippedExisting: 0,
+      skippedInvalid: 0,
+      skippedMissingTimes: 0,
+      note: options.timedOut ? 'sync_pending' : 'sync_error',
+      errors: [options.message],
+    },
+  };
+
+  for (const provider of providers) {
+    const key = PROVIDER_KEY_BY_INTEGRATION[provider.id];
+    if (!key) continue;
+    sleepProviders[key] = {
+      ...sleepProviders[key],
+      connected: provider.status?.connected === true,
+      available: provider.status?.connected === true,
+      hasPermissions: provider.status?.connected === true,

+    sleepSynced: false,
+    activitySynced: false,
+    syncedAt: null,

+      sleepWriteSuccesses: 0,
+      sleepSyncStatus: options.timedOut ? 'no_provider' : 'write_failed',
+      ...(options.timedOut ? { sleepWriteErrors: [options.message] } : { saveError: options.message }),
+      sleepProviders,
+    },
+  };

```
diff --git a/DEEP_ANALYSIS_FEEDBACK_2025.md b/DEEP_ANALYSIS_FEEDBACK_2025.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d14d86b
--- /dev/null
+++ b/DEEP_ANALYSIS_FEEDBACK_2025.md
@@ -0,0 +1,201 @@
+# Deep Analysis: User Feedback (Jan 2025)
+
+This document summarizes issues identified from user feedback, root cause analysis, and proposed fixes. **Review and approve before implementation.**
+
+---
+
+## 1. Loading Screen / ReclaimLogo
+
+### Issue
+- **R position**: The "R" appears at the top-left of the orb instead of centered.
+- **Rings**: The rings don't overlap the orb like the logo (splash.png) – they should pass through the central orb.
+
+### Root Cause
+- **R position**: The R path has viewBox ~0–26 × 0–48. Centering uses &#96;translateX: -14, translateY: -24&#96;. The path’s visual center may be off (e.g. left‑heavy). Correct center is likely &#96;-13, -24&#96; or needs to be derived from the path’s bounding box.
+- **Rings**: Rings are drawn as ellipses; render order and/or stroke width may make them appear to sit outside the orb. In the splash, rings visually pass through the central orb.
+
+### Proposed Fix
+1. **R centering**: Measure the R path’s bounding box; use half width and half height for translate values. Or compare with &#96;splash.png&#96; and adjust until the R aligns with the center orb.
+2. **Rings**: Adjust z-order so rings overlap the orb, or increase ring stroke width/opacity so they clearly pass through the center.
+3. **Reference**: Use &#96;splash.png&#96; (or equivalent asset) as the visual reference and align ReclaimLogo to match.
+
+---
+
+## 2. Random Bench / Prep Notifications Without Active Session
+
+### Issue
+Training “bench start” (or similar) notifications fire when no session is running.
+
+### Root Cause
+1. **Stale intents**: If the user force-closes or navigates away during a guided session without completing or cancelling, intents remain. The next &#96;reconcileNotifications&#96; can still schedule them, and OS notifications can fire later.
+2. **Missing &#96;training_first&#96; clear**: Session end clears &#96;training_rest:&#96; and &#96;training_set:&#96; but not &#96;training_first:&#96;. The “Session started” intent (&#96;training_first:&#96;) is not cleared on session end (though it usually fires immediately).
+3. **No startup cleanup**: There is no app startup cleanup that clears training intents when there is no in-progress session.
+
+### Proposed Fix
+1. **Clear &#96;training_first&#96; on session end**: In &#96;TrainingSessionView&#96; (handleComplete and handleCancelSession), also call &#96;clearIntentsByPrefix(\&#96;training_first:\${sessionId}:\&#96;)&#96;.
+2. **Startup/foreground cleanup**: On app launch or foreground, if there is no in-progress training session, call &#96;clearIntentsByPrefix('training_rest:')&#96;, &#96;clearIntentsByPrefix('training_set:')&#96;, &#96;clearIntentsByPrefix('training_first:')&#96;, then &#96;reconcileNotifications()&#96;. This removes stale training intents and cancels orphaned notifications.
+
+---
+
+## 3. Mood Screen Hero – Text Cut Off, Drawing Too Small
+
+### Issue
+- Hero text is cut off.
+- Hero drawing (MoodWeatherVisualization) is smaller than on other screens (e.g. Sleep, Meds).
+
+### Root Cause
+- MoodHero uses the same constants as SleepHero (e.g. &#96;ORB_WIDTH_RATIO&#96;, &#96;ORB_MIN&#96;, &#96;ORB_MAX&#96;, &#96;centerSize = orbSize * 0.70&#96;), but MoodScreen layout or content may differ.
+- Text overflow: title at &#96;top: 28&#96; with &#96;variant="titleLarge"&#96; may be clipped if the container has &#96;overflow: hidden&#96; or insufficient height.
+- Diagram height &#96;DIAGRAM_SIZE = 390&#96; might be too small for content on some devices.
+
+### Proposed Fix
+1. Align MoodHero with SleepHero and MedsHero: use the same orb/ring sizing and center size.
+2. Ensure the hero container uses &#96;overflow: 'visible'&#96; and avoid clipping the title.
+3. Ensure title and context text use &#96;numberOfLines&#96; and &#96;ellipsizeMode&#96; only if truncation is desired; otherwise increase height or adjust layout.
+4. Consider increasing &#96;PADDING_TOP&#96; or using &#96;minHeight&#96; so the full title and subtitle fit.
+
+---
+
+## 4. Meds Screen Hero – Text Cut Off
+
+### Issue
+Meds hero text is cut off (similar to Mood).
+
+### Root Cause
+Same structural issues as Mood hero: layout and sizing not matching other screens.
+
+### Proposed Fix
+1. Match MedsHero layout to SleepHero (e.g. orb size, ring ratios, center size).
+2. Add &#96;overflow: 'visible'&#96; and adjust padding/height so title and context lines are not clipped.
+3. Verify text containers have enough space; increase &#96;PADDING_TOP&#96; if needed.
+
+---
+
+## 5. Meds Showing “High Consistency” When Not Taking Regularly
+
+### Issue
+Insight “meds-high-consistency” appears and meds adherence looks high even when the user has not been taking medications regularly.
+
+### Root Cause
+- &#96;computeAdherence(logs)&#96; uses:
+  - &#96;scheduled = logs.length&#96;
+  - &#96;taken = logs.filter(l =&gt; l.status === 'taken').length&#96;
+  - &#96;pct = taken / scheduled&#96;
+- &#96;meds_log&#96; only contains user-recorded events (Taken/Skip). There are no automatic “missed” rows.
+- So if a user logs 6 taken doses in 7 days, we get 6 logs, 6 taken → 100% adherence.
+- The real expectation is: **expected doses from schedule** vs **taken**. With 14 expected (e.g. 2/day × 7) and 6 taken, adherence should be ~43%, not 100%.
+
+### Proposed Fix
+1. Change &#96;computeAdherence&#96; to be schedule-based:
+   - New function: &#96;computeAdherenceFromSchedule(logs, meds)&#96;:
+     - &#96;expected =&#96; sum over meds of &#96;upcomingDoseTimes(med.schedule, N)&#96; for the last N days (count only past doses).
+     - &#96;taken =&#96; logs with &#96;status === 'taken'&#96; in that window.
+     - &#96;pct = expected &gt; 0 ? round((taken / expected) * 100) : 0&#96;
+2. Update Dashboard, contextBuilder, and MedsScreen to pass &#96;meds&#96; (and date window) into adherence computation.
+3. Fallback: if we can’t compute expected from schedule (e.g. no meds), use current behavior but document it as best-effort.
+
+---
+
+## 6. Meds Screen Layout – Too Text-Heavy and Redundant
+
+### Issue
+- “Due today” shows meds, times, and days under the header.
+- “Active medications” below repeats similar data.
+- Layout feels cluttered and text-heavy.
+
+### Proposed Redesign Options
+
+**Option A – Single “Today” Card**
+- One card: “Today’s medications”
+- Each med: name, dose, times (e.g. “8:00 AM, 9:00 PM”), days (e.g. “Mon–Fri”).
+- Per-dose row: time | Taken / Skip / Missed (actionable).
+- Remove a separate “Active medications” section, or move it to a collapsible “All medications” area.
+
+**Option B – Swipeable Dose Cards**
+- One card per dose slot today (chronological).
+- Each card: med name, time, status (Due / Taken / Skipped), quick actions.
+- “Active medications” becomes a compact list (names + times) without duplicating dose details.
+
+**Option C – Timeline View**
+- Vertical timeline for today.
+- Each slot: time, med(s) at that time, status, tap to log.
+- “Manage medications” link to add/edit meds.
+- Less repetition, clearer at-a-glance view.
+
+**Recommendation**: Option A or C to reduce duplication and make actions clearer.
+
+---
+
+## 7. App Crashes on Navigate / Certain Actions
+
+### Issue
+The app sometimes closes when navigating or performing actions.
+
+### Root Cause (Hypotheses)
+- Unhandled JS exceptions (partially mitigated by error boundaries and Sentry).
+- React Navigation stack issues or invalid routes.
+- Heavy work on the main thread during navigation.
+- Native module or Skia/Canvas errors (e.g. in hero diagrams).
+
+### Proposed Fix
+1. Ensure &#96;ScreenErrorBoundary&#96; wraps all main screens (Dashboard, Exercise, Mood, Sleep, Meds).
+2. Add Sentry breadcrumbs for navigation events.
+3. Review &#96;navigation.navigate()&#96; and route params; guard against undefined routes or invalid params.
+4. Add &#96;try/catch&#96; and error logging around likely crash points (e.g. hero renders, chart components).
+5. If Skia is suspected, isolate hero rendering with an error boundary.
+
+---
+
+## 8. Dashboard Mood Node – Not Linked to Brain, Shows “Off” When It Should Show “On”
+
+### Issue
+- Mood chip is not visually linked to the brain like Sleep, Meds, Training.
+- Mood shows as “off” even when there is mood data.
+
+### Root Cause
+1. **Connector**: &#96;NodeToBrainConnectors&#96; draws lines for &#96;['mood', 'sleep', 'training', 'meds', 'insights']&#96;. Mood is included, so the connector should render. If it appears unlinked, it may be due to color (&#96;isActive ? color : dim&#96;) – when status is &#96;'—'&#96;, the line is dim.
+2. **Status**: &#96;getLifecycleNodeStatuses&#96; uses &#96;mood: moodStreakCount &gt;= 1 ? 'steady' : '—'&#96;. So mood is active only when &#96;moodStreakCount &gt;= 1&#96; (consecutive days).
+3. **Mismatch**: User may have mood check-ins but no streak (e.g. non-consecutive days), so &#96;moodStreakCount === 0&#96; → status &#96;'—'&#96; → dim connector and “off” look.
+
+### Proposed Fix
+1. Broaden mood status: treat mood as active if there is any mood data in the last 7 days (e.g. &#96;hasMoodCheckinsLast7Days&#96;), not only when &#96;moodStreakCount &gt;= 1&#96;.
+2. Extend &#96;getLifecycleNodeStatuses&#96; with &#96;hasMoodCheckinsRecent?: boolean&#96; and use: &#96;mood: (moodStreakCount &gt;= 1 || hasMoodCheckinsRecent) ? 'steady' : '—'&#96;.
+3. In Dashboard, compute &#96;hasMoodCheckinsRecent&#96; (e.g. from &#96;listMoodCheckins&#96; or an existing query) and pass it into &#96;getLifecycleNodeStatuses&#96;.
+
+---
+
+## 9. Log Analysis (From Provided Events)
+
+### Observations
+- &#96;insight_shown&#96; events repeat (e.g. &#96;meds-high-consistency&#96;, &#96;mood-below-baseline&#96;) across dashboard, meds, and mood screens.
+- &#96;sync_coordinator_completed&#96; with &#96;sleepSyncStatus: "synced"&#96; or &#96;"write_failed"&#96; – sync flow appears to run as designed.
+- Multiple rapid &#96;insight_shown&#96; events suggest duplicate renders or multiple insight cards being evaluated in quick succession.
+
+### Potential Actions
+1. Add idempotency or debouncing for insight display to avoid duplicate logs.
+2. Ensure insight selection runs once per screen mount/focus, not on every render.
+3. Re-check &#96;meds-high-consistency&#96; display once adherence logic is fixed (Issue 5).
+
+---
+
+## Implementation Priority
+
+| # | Issue                       | Priority | Effort |
+|---|-----------------------------|----------|--------|
+| 5 | Meds adherence logic        | High     | Medium |
+| 2 | Training notifications      | High     | Low    |
+| 8 | Mood node status/connector  | High     | Low    |
+| 3 | Mood hero sizing/cutoff     | Medium   | Low    |
+| 4 | Meds hero cutoff            | Medium   | Low    |
+| 1 | ReclaimLogo R + rings       | Medium   | Medium |
+| 6 | Meds screen redesign        | Medium   | High   |
+| 7 | App crashes                 | High     | Medium |
+
+---
+
+## Next Steps
+
+1. Review this document and approve or adjust proposed fixes.
+2. Decide on Meds redesign direction (A, B, or C).
+3. Implement in the order above, or as you prefer.
+4. Re-test after each change.

```

   - The duplicate removal logic: it groups by logicalKey - so if we have 2 notifications with same logicalKey but different identifiers, it should keep one and cancel the other. 2. buildNotificationPlan creates mood_morning, mood_evening - and scheduleMoodCheckinReminders ALSO sets intents for mood_morning, mood_evening! So we have TWO sources: buildNotificationPlan (from prefs) and buildPlanFromIntents (from intents). The merge says intents override - so if scheduleMoodCheckinReminders wrote intents, buildPlanFromIntents would produce mood_morning/mood_evening. But buildNotificationPlan ALSO produces them! So in the merge: settings plan first, then intents. So intents override. So we'd only have one mood_morning. But wait - buildNotificationPlan uses getNotificationPreferences and adds mood if moodRemindersEnabled. And scheduleMoodCheckinReminders is a separate function that writes intents. So we have:
   - buildNotificationPlan: adds mood_morning, mood_evening (from prefs)
   - buildPlanFromIntents: adds mood_morning, mood_evening from intents (if scheduleMoodCheckinReminders was called)
   - Merge: byKey.set from settings, then byKey.set from intents - intents override. So we'd get one each.
   - But the fingerprint would include both - and the fingerprint is computed from merged. So we'd have 2 mood notifications in merged. That's correct - one morning, one evening.

So duplicates of same logicalKey should be removed. Unless... the planSignature differs? For med reminders, the trigger might have `date` or `seconds` - and the planSignature includes that. If seconds changes (e.g. reconcile runs at different times), the signature would differ! For Android, med reminders use seconds. Each time reconcile runs, `now` changes, so `seconds` changes - so the planned notification has a different trigger each run. That means planSignature differs every time! So we'd cancel the old one and schedule a new one - that could cause flickering but not duplicates. Unless we're scheduling MULTIPLE notifications with different logicalKeys for the same conceptual reminder? Like med:123:08:00 and med:123:08:00:snooze - those are different keys.
   
4. When could we get duplicates?

   - If multiple components call scheduleMedReminderActionable for the same dose - we have isAlreadyScheduled check
   - If buildNotificationPlan and buildPlanFromIntents both produce the same logicalKey - we merge, so only one
   - Med reminders: each dose is med:medId:doseTimeISO. If quiet hours changes doseTimeISO, we'd have old intent (med:123:08:00) and new (med:123:08:15). The old one wouldn't be cleared - we'd have TWO! The med scheduling might not clear the old intent when rescheduling.

  "plan": "# Notification System Fixes\n\n## Assessment: Rewrite vs. Fix\n\n**Recommendation: Fix the existing system.** The architecture (NotificationScheduler + NotificationIntentStore + reconcile) is sound. This can cause flicker and multiple “same” notifications if reconcile runs often.\n- **Mitigation:** Ensure reconcile is not triggered too frequently (debounce, cooldown). Current debounce is 250ms; cooldown in useNotifications is 5s. May need to avoid reconciling med reminders when their trigger would only change by a few seconds.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Training Not Firing Correctly\n\n**Cause A – No daily “time to train” reminder**\n\n- &#96;TRAINING_REMINDER&#96; is only created from intents when the user snoozes (e.g. &#96;training_snooze:identifier&#96;).\n- There is **no code** that schedules the initial daily “time to train today” reminder.\n- The [TrainingScreen](app/src/screens/TrainingScreen.tsx) computes &#96;nextSession&#96; but never writes a TRAINING_REMINDER intent for it.\n- **Fix:** Add logic (e.g. in SyncCoordinator, TrainingScreen, or a training-specific scheduler) to:\n  - Detect when the user has a session today.\n  - Write a &#96;training_reminder:sessionId&#96; or similar intent with &#96;triggerDate&#96; (e.g. user’s preferred time or a default like 9:00).\n  - Let &#96;buildPlanFromIntents&#96; schedule it via the existing &#96;TRAINING_REMINDER&#96; path.\n\n**Cause B – In-session rest/set notifications (training_rest, training_set)**\n\n- These are scheduled by [TrainingSessionView](app/src/components/training/TrainingSessionView.tsx) via &#96;scheduleTrainingRest&#96; and &#96;scheduleTrainingSet&#96;.\n- Possible issues:\n  - &#96;clearStaleTrainingIntentsIfNoActiveSession&#96; may clear intents too aggressively (e.g. network timeout → “no active session” → intents cleared).\n  - Android &#96;timeInterval&#96; trigger with &#96;seconds&#96; can be unreliable; worth checking expo-notifications behavior.\n- **Investigation:** Add diagnostics to confirm whether rest/set intents are written and whether reconcile picks them up. If intents exist but notifications don’t fire, the problem is in the trigger/scheduling layer.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Missing Notifications\n\n**Possible causes:**\n\n- Permission denied or revoked.\n- Channels not created (Android).\n- Fingerprint short-circuit: if fingerprint matches and all keys “appear” present, reconcile skips. A bug in the “keys present” check could skip rescheduling after system clears notifications.\n- BuildPlanFromIntents skips past-due: &#96;when \u003c oneHourAgo&#96; for med reminders; &#96;when \u003c= new Date()&#96; for meditation after-wake. Legitimate near-term notifications might be skipped if time logic is wrong.\n- &#96;reconciling&#96; mutex: rapid calls could cause some reconcile runs to be skipped; debouncing should help, but worth ensuring no important trigger is lost.\n\n---\n\n## Implementation Plan\n\n### Phase 1: Med duplicate fix (high impact, low risk)\n\n1. In &#96;refreshReminderStatus&#96; / &#96;scheduleAllSilent&#96; (MedsScreen), clear all med intents before scheduling:\n   - Add &#96;clearIntentsByPrefix('med:')&#96; before the loop over meds, **or**\n   - Before each &#96;scheduleForMed(m)&#96;, call &#96;clearIntentsByPrefix(\\&#96;med:${m.id}:\\&#96;)&#96;.\n2. Prefer per-med clear inside &#96;scheduleForMed&#96; (in &#96;useMedReminderScheduler&#96;) so every call path (MedsScreen, MedDetailsScreen, Settings) is consistent.\n\n### Phase 2: Daily training reminder (high impact, medium risk)\n\n1. Add a function (e.g. in &#96;trainingNotificationScheduler.ts&#96; or a new &#96;trainingReminderScheduler.ts&#96;):\n   - Input: today’s session (if any), user’s preferred reminder time (from settings or default 9:00).\n   - Write intent: &#96;training_reminder:${sessionId}&#96; or &#96;training_reminder:${programDayId}&#96; with &#96;type: 'TRAINING_REMINDER'&#96;, &#96;triggerDate&#96;, &#96;sessionId&#96;, etc.\n2. Call this from:\n   - TrainingScreen when &#96;nextSession&#96; exists and is today, or\n   - SyncCoordinator after training sync, or\n   - A dedicated effect when training data loads.\n3. Clear the intent when the session is completed or when there’s no session today (to avoid stale reminders).\n\n### Phase 3: Reconcile stability and diagnostics\n\n1. **Med Android trigger:** Consider using &#96;date&#96; instead of &#96;seconds&#96; for med reminders on Android to avoid signature churn, if expo-notifications supports it for near-term dates.\n2. **Diagnostics:** Ensure DiagnosticsScreen or a debug path can show: scheduled count, intent count, and a sample of logical keys. Here’s how your setup lines up with the guidelines and what’s likely causing the watch behavior.

## 1. Do you follow the guidelines?

From the Android docs and your code:

| Guideline | Status |
|-----------|--------|
| **POST_NOTIFICATIONS** (Android 13+) | ✅ You use `expo-notifications`; permission is usually handled. |
| **Notification channels** | ✅ `ensureReclaimChannels()` creates channels with sensible importance before posting. |
| **Basic notification** | ✅ `NotificationCompat`-style usage via expo; small icon, title, body, content intent. |
| **Category / actions** | ✅ `MED_REMINDER`, `TRAINING_REMINDER`, etc. with actions. |
| **Action options** | ✅ `opensAppToForeground: false` for Taken / Snooze / Skip so actions run in background. |

So your code is generally in line with the guidelines.

The problems you’re seeing (duplicates, missing training reminders, watch “going to phone”) come from logic and flow, not from violating basic Android notification rules.

## 2. Fix vs rewrite: recommended direction

**Recommendation: fix the current implementation, don’t rewrite.**

- Your structure (channels, categories, actions) is correct.
- A rewrite would mostly change orchestration, not Android usage.
- The remaining issues are targeted bugs that can be fixed in place.

## 3. Why the watch is taking you to the phone

This comes from **Wear OS bridging** and how the default tap is handled.

From the [Bridging options for notifications](https://developer.android.com/training/wearables/notifications/bridger) doc:

> “If you are using bridged notifications, any notification automatically includes a button to launch the app on the phone.”

So for bridged notifications:

- Your notification is created on the phone and bridged to the watch.
- Wear adds a system **“Open on phone”** affordance (e.g. button or primary tap behavior).
- The default tap may be mapped to the content intent (`setContentIntent`), which opens the app on the phone.

Your action buttons (Taken, Snooze, Skip) use `opensAppToForeground: false`, so they should run in the background. But:

1. The **default tap** (notification body, not an action button) still uses the content intent.
2. On Wear, tapping the notification card often triggers that content intent, which opens the app on the phone.

If you want “tap on watch” to mark Taken and sync to the phone without switching to the phone:

- You’d need the default tap to be treated like an action (e.g. TAKE) that runs in the background.
- With expo-notifications and bridging, the default tap is usually the content intent, which opens the app. That’s why the watch sends you to the phone on tap.

So the “watch takes me to phone” behavior is largely driven by how Wear handles the content intent on bridged notifications, not by a misconfiguration of your action buttons.

## 4. Wear OS 5 and bridging changes

From the docs:

> “Some notifications that are dismissible on a mobile device aren’t dismissible on the Wear OS device.”

If you also have a standalone Wear app and create local notifications on the watch, you can get:

- Duplicate notifications on the watch (bridged + local).
- Different default behaviors.

The doc suggests using the [Bridging APIs](https://developer.android.com/training/wearables/notifications/bridger) to control bridging and avoid duplicates (e.g. `setBridgeTag()`, `BridgingConfig`, or disabling bridging where appropriate).

## 5. Concrete next steps

1. **Med duplicates**  
   Add the clear-before-reschedule logic in `scheduleForMed` / bulk scheduling as in the plan.

2. **Missing training reminders**  
   Add a daily training reminder intent and scheduling path so those reminders are created at all.

3. **Watch “opens phone” on tap**  
   - Keep using action buttons for Taken / Snooze / Skip; they’re configured correctly.
   - Document that the default tap opens the app on the phone (standard for bridged notifications).
   - If you want tap-to-mark-taken without opening the phone, that would likely require native changes or a different UX (e.g. only using action buttons, or a custom Wear notification).

4. **Wear OS bridging (if you have a watch app)**  
   - Check if you create notifications on both phone and watch.
   - Use Bridging APIs to avoid duplicates and to control what appears on the watch.

**Bottom line:** your code aligns with the Android notification guidelines. The issues are about orchestration and Wear bridging. Focus on the targeted fixes in the plan; a full rewrite is not necessary.
